explanation: The ECU watches how fast the upstream oxygen sensor switches between lean and rich, and found it is switching too slowly — a lazy sensor. The code does not say whether the sensor itself is worn, the exhaust is leaking ahead of it, or the wiring is at fault.

initial_hypotheses.label: Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

repairs.label: Replace upstream O2 sensor (bank 1, sensor 1)
repairs.verification: Rescan after a drive cycle; confirm the switching rate is back above ~8 switches per 10 s at 2,500 RPM and P0133 stays clear.

repairs.label: Repair exhaust manifold gasket / leak ahead of the O2 sensor
repairs.verification: Rescan; confirm O2 switching rate and amplitude normalize and P0133 stays clear.

repairs.label: Repair O2 sensor wiring / connector
repairs.verification: Wiggle-test the harness while watching live O2 data; confirm P0133 stays clear over 2+ drive cycles.

safety.stop_message: Stop driving and seek professional service.

tests.question: Hold a steady 2,500 RPM and count upstream O2 sensor switches (lean-rich crossings) over 10 seconds, and note the voltage amplitude.
Any ticking exhaust leak, soot marks, or broken manifold hardware ahead of the upstream O2 sensor?
Is the O2 sensor wiring chafed, melted, or oil-soaked, or is the connector corroded or loose?

title: O2 sensor circuit slow response (bank 1, sensor 1)
